title: "I fired my $2K/mo editor — this free AI does it better"
description: Creator tears a printed invoice on camera, then demos one free AI editing tool cutting this exact video; ends on a self-referential twist.
why_it_works: Money + an enemy in the first 2 seconds; the twist ("this tool edited what you just watched") converts a saturated listicle into proof.

title: "3 AI tools that feel illegal to know" — screen-rec listicle
hook_text: These 3 AI tools feel illegal to know
description: Faceless screen recording, cursor-led demos of three niche AI tools, captions bottom-third, hard cuts every 6s.
why_it_works: Forbidden-knowledge framing plus zero-face production the audience can replicate; save-the-list utility drives saves.

title: "POV: you automate your job in 60 seconds" — avatar explainer
hook_text: POV: your boss doesn't know you automated 80% of your job
description: AI-avatar talking head walks through a no-code automation, split screen with the workflow running live.
why_it_works: POV framing puts the viewer inside a mildly transgressive win; split-screen proof keeps retention through the demo.

title: "Human editor vs AI — same clip, who wins?" — challenge format
hook_text: I gave the same footage to a pro editor and an AI
description: Side-by-side edit race with a countdown timer; comment-bait ending asks viewers to vote which cut wins.
why_it_works: Versus structure creates a built-in payoff and a comment mechanic (vote), lifting both retention and engagement.

title: "Day 12 of building a startup with only AI" — series diary
hook_text: Day 12: the AI just saved me a $4,000 mistake
description: Serialized founder diary; each episode opens with the day number and one win or disaster, ends foreshadowing the next episode.
why_it_works: Serialization converts viewers into followers — the day-number pattern trains the audience to come back.

title: "Your $80 serum has 2% actives — check the label" — UGC callout
hook_text: Your $80 serum has 2% of the thing you bought it for
description: Selfie UGC, creator flips a premium bottle to its ingredient label, price-anchors against a budget alternative, patch-test cutaway as proof.
why_it_works: Loss framing on money already spent; the label flip is a physical pattern-interrupt that works on mute.

title: Meta Ad Library — ingredient-callout skincare ad, 94 days live
description: Longest-running skincare ad in the sample set: PAS structure, on-screen ingredient percentages, single CTA to 'check your label'.
why_it_works: 94 days of continuous spend is revealed preference — the ingredient-percentage overlay is the proof element that sustains CTR.

title: "My derm's 3-word advice" — testimonial story
hook_text: My dermatologist said three words that changed my skin
description: Story-led testimonial withholding the three words until 0:18; text overlay reveal, before/after cutaways.
why_it_works: A concrete withheld payoff (three words) is a stronger open loop than a generic promise; authority borrowed from the derm.

title: Side-by-side texture test, no talking — ASMR product demo
description: No-VO ASMR demo: two serums spread side by side on glass, captions carry the comparison, loops seamlessly.
why_it_works: Sensory loop with zero language barrier; the seamless loop inflates watch time past 100%.

title: "I tracked every rupee for 30 days" — data-diary
hook_text: I tracked every single rupee I spent for 30 days
description: Animated spend-tracker screen recording with day-counter; ends with one counterintuitive takeaway and next-episode tease.
why_it_works: Quantified-self commitment device; the animated tracker gives constant visual progression that holds retention.

title: "Things in my kitchen that are secretly protein" — listicle
hook_text: 5 things in your kitchen that are secretly 20g of protein
description: Fast-cut fridge raid, each item gets a protein-count overlay; save-the-list CTA.
why_it_works: Utility listicle with numeric overlays — the save rate carries distribution more than likes.

title: "POV: first day at the gym and everyone's nice" — skit
hook_text: POV: it's your first gym day and everyone is actually nice
description: Wholesome inversion skit of gym-intimidation tropes; multiple characters played by one creator.
why_it_works: Subverts a feared scenario into a warm one — identity-affirming shares ('tag your gym buddy').

title: "₹120 street thali vs ₹1200 hotel thali" — comparison
hook_text: Same thali. One costs 10x more. Which wins?
description: Price-anchored taste test with blindfold reveal; on-screen scorecard per dish.
why_it_works: Price-versus framing plus a scorecard structure gives the viewer a game to play along with.

title: "I wore the same outfit formula for a week" — style experiment
hook_text: One outfit formula, seven days, zero thinking
description: Daily transition cuts on the same formula (jacket/tee/trouser), ends with a save-able formula card.
why_it_works: Formula framing makes fashion feel replicable; the end-card is engineered for saves.

title: "Unboxing our worst review" — brand self-roast UGC
hook_text: We printed our worst 1-star review on the box
description: Brand account unboxes a package printed with its own 1-star review, then addresses it point by point with receipts.
why_it_works: Self-roast disarms skepticism; answering the objection on camera is persuasion disguised as entertainment.

title: "AI news in 45 seconds, no hype" — anchor-style recap
hook_text: Everything that mattered in AI this week — no hype
description: Anchor-style weekly recap with lower-third headlines, strict 3-story structure, anti-hype positioning.
why_it_works: The 'no hype' promise is differentiation in a saturated news niche; fixed structure builds appointment viewing.

title: "We put our product through airport security 10 times" — stress test ad
hook_text: TSA has now scanned this bag 10 times. Still perfect.
description: Durability stress-test montage with a running counter overlay; ends on warranty CTA.
why_it_works: Repetition counter turns durability (a boring claim) into a visual game; concrete proof beats adjectives.

title: "Rating AI thumbnails my subscribers made" — community format
hook_text: You made AI thumbnails for my video. Some of you went too far.
description: Creator rates audience-submitted AI-generated thumbnails on a scorecard; winner's thumbnail actually gets used.
why_it_works: Audience-sourced content creates a submission loop — every episode recruits participants for the next.
